beliefs: The box reverses the order of characters in the input string [E1]
Reversal preserves case, digits, punctuation, and spaces exactly, only order changes [E1]
All leading spaces (0x20) are stripped from the input before reversal; leading tabs/newlines are kept [E14, E13, E11]
Trailing whitespace of all kinds is stripped from the input before reversal [E6, E7, E10, E12]
After reversal, leading whitespace of all kinds is stripped from the result [E7, E10]
Equivalently: strip all leading spaces, strip trailing whitespace (all kinds), reverse, then strip leading whitespace (all kinds) from the result [E14, E13]
notes: E14 shows all leading spaces are stripped (not just one), and E13 shows leading tabs/newlines are preserved, so the rule is lstrip(' ') then rstrip() then reverse then lstrip().
